sources.title: Full text of Sankara's 1984 UN General Assembly address
"A United Front Against the Debt" -- Sankara's 1987 speech before the OAU

Historical accounts of his 1983-1987 presidency of Burkina Faso, including quantified vaccination/literacy/tree-planting figures, his personal austerity measures, and his women's-rights and land-reform policies

leadership_drive.rationale: Directed a comprehensive, quantified, multi-domain national reform program across health (a vaccination campaign reaching an estimated 2.5 million children in roughly two weeks, cutting infant mortality from 208 to 145 per 1,000 within one year), education (literacy rising from 13% in 1983 to 73% in 1987, 350+ communities building their own schools), and environment (over 10 million trees planted), all sustained simultaneously across his roughly four-year presidency, documented via the well-corroborated historical record of these specific, dated programs and their measured outcomes.

proactive_agency.rationale: Multiple self-initiated, unprompted personal actions with no external requirement: sold the government's Mercedes-Benz fleet for the cheapest available car, capped his own presidential salary to the average civil-servant wage ($450/month), and publicly disclosed his full personal asset list, documented via the well-corroborated historical record of these specific, voluntary acts.

independent_thinking.rationale: Two independent, dated, primary-source-documented speeches sustaining the same structural argument against prevailing international consensus: his October 1984 UN General Assembly address explicitly rejecting foreign-aid dependency, and his 1987 OAU address arguing that African debt was a direct continuation of colonial control ("the same ones who used to manage our states and economies... indebted Africa") -- a sustained, consistent ideological position held across separate international forums over several years, not a single speech.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Two independent, directly documented confrontational public acts: the 1984 UN speech and the 1987 OAU speech each explicitly and publicly antagonized the specific creditor nations and institutions his own country depended on for aid, alongside domestic land reforms that directly abolished the feudal privileges of traditional tribal chieftaincies -- sustained willingness to remain in conflict with powerful interests on multiple fronts simultaneously, rather than moderate his position.

impact_motivation.rationale: Measured, population-level impact converging across three independent domains within a single four-year tenure: infant mortality nearly halved (208 to 145 per 1,000), national literacy roughly quintupled (13% to 73%), and over 10 million trees planted under a mandatory participation policy -- documented via the specific, quantified historical record of each program.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Delivered direct, public, confrontational rhetoric against powerful creditor nations and international financial institutions his own country depended on for aid, and directly abolished the feudal land privileges of traditional tribal chieftaincies within his own country -- documented via the specific content of his UN and OAU speeches and his land-reform policy record; this row is scored from those documented actions themselves, not from his 1987 assassination, which is recorded as biographical context only.

achievement_drive.rationale: Implemented a sweeping, multi-domain reform program (land, health, literacy, environment, women's rights, anti-corruption) within roughly four years in office, inferred as exceptional achievement drive from the documented scope, pace, and now-quantified scale of these changes relative to the short time available.

execution_speed.rationale: Two independent, quantified, rapid-execution episodes: a vaccination campaign reaching an estimated 2.5 million children in roughly two weeks, and a 500-unit housing program completed within three months, both documented via specific, dated program figures.

persuasiveness.rationale: His surviving speeches, including the 1984 UN address, are widely cited by later historians as rhetorically forceful and are credited with raising his international profile substantially, inferred as real persuasive skill from the documented reach and later frequent citation of these speeches.

resourcefulness.rationale: Sold off the government's fleet of Mercedes-Benz vehicles in favor of the cheaper Renault 5 as the official ministerial car, and mandated that civil servants wear domestically-woven cotton fabric (Faso Dan Fani) rather than imported textiles specifically to support local industry, inferred as genuinely resourceful, symbolically-deliberate governance from the convergence of these two independently-documented concrete measures.

planning_orientation.rationale: Multiple independent, structured-program-design instances: a mandatory tree-planting policy explicitly tied to social-aid eligibility (from 1985), dedicated new institutional infrastructure for a policy goal (a Ministry of Family Development and the Women's Union of Burkina, established in his first year specifically to support the women's-rights agenda), and a constitutional amendment requiring at least five women ministers in cabinet at all times.

discipline.rationale: Sustained, self-imposed personal austerity maintained consistently throughout his tenure rather than as a one-off gesture: capped his own salary to the average civil-servant wage, refused government chauffeurs and air-conditioned offices, and publicly disclosed his complete personal asset list, documented via the specific, itemized historical record of these measures.

collaboration.rationale: Over 350 communities built their own schools with their own labor as part of the national literacy campaign, a single documented instance of a deliberately participatory rather than top-down program design.

adaptability.rationale: Moved from a military career into national civilian governance and rapid multi-domain policy implementation within a short period, inferred as requiring real adaptability from the documented scope of this transition, though the specific evidence for this trait beyond the transition itself is comparatively thin.

curiosity.rationale: Was a trained military pilot and an accomplished amateur guitarist alongside his political career, inferred as some real range of personal interest beyond politics from these documented, distinct pursuits.

detail_orientation.rationale: Personally required detailed government asset declarations from ministers as part of his anti-corruption program, and itemized his own personal assets down to specific counted possessions, inferred as real attention to administrative detail from the documented specificity of both practices.

portrait.reason: Widely-circulated archival photographs found lack a clearly confirmed Public Domain or CC license on Commons; not independently verified this session.

provenance.notes: Roster-1000 session 13 (source-grounded research-depth control): re-researched from session 12's original 3-source, 12-row profile using genuinely inspected substantive sources, including the primary full text of both his 1984 UN and 1987 OAU speeches and quantified historical accounts of his vaccination/literacy/tree-planting/women's-rights programs. A factual evidence ledger (12 distinct new/refined episodes) was built and locked before any trait score was assigned; NEW_EVIDENCE per docs/scoring-rubric-v1.md Sec.10. All 12 of the original session-12 rows are retained (several substantially strengthened in confidence/evidenceType by newly-inspected quantified sources, e.g. leadership_drive strong_inference 0.48 -> documented 0.75); 4 new rows were added (proactive_agency, execution_speed, discipline, collaboration) from genuinely distinct newly-researched facts not previously captured. His 1987 assassination is noted as biographical context only -- the risk_tolerance row is explicitly scored from his own documented confrontational actions and speeches, not from the assassination itself, per CLAUDE.md's Safety discipline against deriving a trait score from what was done TO a person.
